originalNodes.title: Addition
originalNodes.goal: Add numbers up to 100 quickly and surely.
originalNodes.kid_text: Adding means putting groups together to find how many you have in all. If you have 5 stickers and a friend gives you 3 more, count on: six, seven, eight, so you have 8! You can add in any order, so 3 + 5 also makes 8. A tens trick helps: 8 + 5 is the same as 10 + 3, which is 13.

lesson_media.alt: A ten-frame holds eight blue pebbles and two of five green counters; three green counters remain below.
lesson_media.caption: Use 2 from the 5 to complete ten; 3 remain, so 8 + 5 = 13.

lesson_media.title: Make a friendly ten
lesson_media.instructions: Move counters from one addend to fill the ten-frame. Swap the addends and notice that the total stays the same.

quiz.say: Five plus three. Is it 7, 8, or 9?
quiz.explain: Count on from five: six, seven, eight!

quiz.say: Eight plus five. Is it 12, 13, or 14?
quiz.explain: Eight and two make ten, and three more makes thirteen.

quiz.say: Twenty plus thirty. Is it 40, 50, or 60?
quiz.explain: Two tens and three tens make five tens, which is fifty.

quiz.say: What is six plus four? 9, 10, or 11?
quiz.explain: Six and four make a friendly ten.

quiz.say: What is seven plus seven? 14, 12, or 15?
quiz.explain: Double seven is fourteen.

quiz.say: What is twenty-five plus ten? 30, 45, or 35?
quiz.explain: Twenty-five is two tens and five ones. One more ten makes three tens and five ones: thirty-five.

quiz.say: Three plus six is nine. So what is six plus three? 9, 6, or 8?
quiz.explain: Swapping the two numbers round never changes the answer, so 6 + 3 is 9 as well.

originalNodes.title: Subtraction
originalNodes.goal: Take away and find the difference.
originalNodes.kid_text: Subtraction is taking some away and counting what is left. If you have 9 grapes and eat 4, then 5 grapes are still waiting. It also answers "how many more?": if you have 9 and a friend has 4, you have 5 more. Subtraction undoes adding, so because 4 + 5 = 9, we know 9 - 4 = 5.

quiz.say: Nine take away four. Is it 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: You had nine grapes, ate four, and five are still waiting.

quiz.say: You have seven sweets and you eat two of them. How many are left? 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: Seven take away two leaves five sweets.

quiz.prompt: You have 10, friend has 6. How many more?
quiz.say: You have ten stickers and your friend has six. How many more do you have? 3, 4, or 5?
quiz.explain: Ten take away six is four, so you have four more.

quiz.say: What is eight take away three? 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: Start at eight and count back three: seven, six, five.

quiz.say: There were six birds and two flew away. How many are left? 4, 3, or 8?
quiz.explain: Six take away two leaves four birds sitting there.

quiz.say: What is twelve take away five? 6, 8, or 7?
quiz.explain: Twelve minus five leaves seven.

quiz.say: Six plus three is nine. So what is nine take away three? 3, 6, or 9?
quiz.explain: Taking away undoes adding, so you land back on six.

lesson_media.alt: Nine counters with four crossed out leave five; paired rows of nine and four also differ by five.
lesson_media.caption: The equation 9 − 4 = 5 can describe what remains or the difference between two quantities. Addition checks the result because 4 + 5 = 9.

lesson_media.title: Take away, see what stays
lesson_media.instructions: Choose how many counters stay and how many are removed. Read the subtraction from the whole group.

originalNodes.title: Place Value
originalNodes.goal: Know what each digit in a big number means.
originalNodes.kid_text: In a big number, where a digit sits tells you how much it is worth. In 47, the 4 means 4 tens, which is forty, and the 7 means 7 ones. So 47 is really 40 and 7 packed together. The digit itself does not grow: moving it one place left makes its place value ten times as large.

quiz.say: In the number forty-seven, what is the four worth? 4, 40, or 400?
quiz.explain: The four sits in the tens spot, so it means four tens, which is forty.

quiz.say: How many tens are hiding inside sixty? 6, 16, or 60?
quiz.explain: Six tens stack up to make sixty.

quiz.say: Forty and seven packed together. Is it 47, 74, or 11?
quiz.explain: Forty and seven make forty-seven.

quiz.say: In the number fifty-eight, how much is the eight worth? 8, 80, or 58?
quiz.explain: The 8 is in the ones place, so it is worth just 8. The 5 is the one worth 50.

quiz.say: How many tens are inside thirty? 30, 3, or 13?
quiz.explain: Thirty is three tens stacked together.

quiz.say: Which number has nine tens in it? 9, 19, or 90?
quiz.explain: Ninety is nine tens, so the nine sits in the tens spot.

quiz.say: What do twenty and six make when you put them together? 62, 206, or 26?
quiz.explain: Two tens and six ones make twenty-six.

lesson_media.alt: Four ten-rods sit in the tens column and seven unit squares sit in the ones column to make 47.
lesson_media.caption: In 47, position gives the 4 a value of forty and the 7 a value of seven. One ten can be exchanged for ten ones without changing the total.

lesson_media.title: Build hundreds, tens and ones
lesson_media.instructions: Change each digit. Compare a hundred square, a ten rod and a single unit; read their contributions to the number.

originalNodes.title: Multiplication
originalNodes.kid_text: Multiplying is a fast way to add the same number again and again. 4 x 3 means 4 groups of 3, so instead of 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 you just know it is 12. Picture 4 rows of 3 cookies on a tray and count them all: 12. Learn your times tables up to 12 x 12 and these answers pop out in a snap.

quiz.say: There are four rows of cookies with three cookies in each row. How many cookies in all? 7, 9, or 12?
quiz.explain: Four groups of three make twelve cookies.

quiz.say: Two times five. Is it 7, 10, or 12?
quiz.explain: Two groups of five make ten.

quiz.say: Six times six. Is it 12, 30, or 36?
quiz.explain: Six rows of six make thirty-six.

quiz.say: What is three times three? 6, 9, or 12?
quiz.explain: Three groups of three make nine.

quiz.say: There are five groups with two sweets in each. How many sweets in all? 10, 7, or 12?
quiz.explain: Two, four, six, eight, ten — five groups of two make ten.

quiz.say: What is twelve times twelve? 124, 144, or 122?
quiz.explain: Twelve twelves make one hundred forty-four, the last one in your tables.

quiz.say: What is seven times two? 14, 16, or 9?
quiz.explain: Two sevens are fourteen, just like seven plus seven.

lesson_media.alt: Four rows of three counters form an array of twelve; turning the array gives three rows of four.
lesson_media.caption: Four groups of three total twelve. Rotating the array shows that 4 × 3 and 3 × 4 have the same product.

lesson_media.title: Rows times columns
lesson_media.instructions: Change the rows and counters in each row. Count equal groups, then compare the product.

originalNodes.title: Division
originalNodes.goal: Share into equal groups; divide with times-table facts.
originalNodes.kid_text: Dividing means sharing a bunch into equal groups so everyone gets the same amount. If you have 12 candies and 3 friends, deal them out one at a time until each friend has 4. Division is the opposite of multiplying: because 3 x 4 = 12, we know 12 / 3 = 4. Your times tables help you share fast!

quiz.say: Twelve candies shared fairly with three friends. How many does each friend get? 3, 4, or 6?
quiz.explain: Deal them out one at a time and each friend gets four.

quiz.say: Ten shared into two equal groups. Is it 4, 5, or 8?
quiz.explain: Ten splits into two equal groups of five.

quiz.say: Three times four is twelve. So twelve divided by four is what? 2, 3, or 4?
quiz.explain: Dividing undoes multiplying, so the answer is three.

quiz.say: What is eight shared into two equal groups? 3, 4, or 6?
quiz.explain: Eight splits fairly into two groups of four.

quiz.say: Six apples go into two baskets, the same in each. How many in one basket? 3, 2, or 4?
quiz.explain: Deal them out one by one and each basket ends with three.

quiz.say: What is twenty shared into five equal groups? 5, 15, or 4?
quiz.explain: Five fours make twenty, so each group gets four.

quiz.say: Five times three is fifteen. So what is fifteen shared into five groups? 5, 3, or 10?
quiz.explain: Dividing undoes multiplying, so the answer is three.

lesson_media.alt: Twelve counters are shared equally among three bowls, leaving four counters in each bowl.
lesson_media.caption: Sharing 12 among 3 equal groups gives 4 in each group. Making groups of 3 from the same 12 instead produces 4 groups.

lesson_media.title: Share equally, count the remainder
lesson_media.instructions: Choose a total and a number of groups. Share whole counters equally and inspect any left over.
